pr_title: fix(elements): update the view of an `OnPush` component when inputs change
pr_body:
As with regular Angular components, Angular elements are expected to have their views update when inputs change.

Previously, Angular Elements views where not update if the underlying component used the `OnPush` change detection strategy.

This commit fixes this by calling `markForCheck()` on the component view's `ChangeDetectorRef`.

NOTE:
This is similar to how `@angular/upgrade` does it: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/3236ae0ee118d0734c90fa9f3767435396213470/packages/upgrade/src/common/src/downgrade_component_adapter.ts#L146.

Fixes #38948.

##
This PR also contains some commit the fix/improve the `elements` tests (both unit and e2e tests). See individual commits for more details.

review_comments:
Would it be relevant to have a test that shows that `markForCheck` is not called if the same value is passed in a new round? Or is this not possible - i.e. would the `strategy.setInputValue()` not even be called in such a case?

Also what about a test that changes the value to something new, and then back to the original value within a single tick. Would that trigger a `markForCheck()`?

Good questions. I've added tests for the first case (setting to the same value in a new round).

For the second case (setting to a new value and then back to the original value), I don't think we'll gain much by adding tests. There is no logic to detect that, so `detectChanges()` (including `markForCheck()`) will run (although redundant 🤷‍♂️).
